criterion: A lint of the toolchain is rejected when a scan should never carry it, for a reason that holds whatever workspace is being scanned. A rejection is a decision, not a backlog: a lint nobody has looked at yet stays in the candidate queue instead of being turned down here.

rejected.reason: Asserts on a literal true or false: the first is dead code the compiler removes, the second is a panic written the long way, and neither changes what a user should fix.
Rewrites a = a + b as a += b, which is shorter and identical in behaviour.
Denied by default in the toolchain: dropping its -W restores Clippy's refusal, so carrying it would turn a scan into a compilation failure instead of a report.
Fires only against a list of types configured in the scanned workspace's own clippy.toml, which a scan neither provides nor should impose.
Rewrites and_then returning Some or Ok as map, which is shorter and identical in behaviour.
Judges the lint configuration a workspace declares for itself, not the code that workspace ships.
A block inside a condition is harder to read, which is a matter of taste rather than a defect.
Rewrites assert_eq against a boolean literal as a plain assert, which is shorter and identical in behaviour.
Rewrites x == true as x, which is shorter and identical in behaviour.
Removes a dereference immediately followed by a borrow, which the compiler already collapses.
Taking a reference to a Box forces the caller to allocate first, which narrows an API without breaking anything it does.
Rewrites Box::new(Default::default()) as Box::default(), which is shorter and identical in behaviour.
Rewrites a slice of byte literals as a byte string, which reads better and compiles to the same bytes.
Rewrites bytes().count() as len(); Clippy files it under complexity because the optimiser usually erases the difference.
Rewrites bytes().nth() as as_bytes().get(), which reads better and avoids walking the iterator.

rust_doctor::structure::complex_function reports the same defect with the same nesting-weighted score, publishes both figures on the diagnostic, and keeps its thresholds under rust-doctor.toml instead of the scanned workspace's clippy.toml.

Inert on an unconfigured workspace: its threshold defaults to zero in the scanned workspace's own clippy.toml, which a scan neither provides nor should impose, and deep nesting already drives the nesting-weighted score of rust_doctor::structure::complex_function.
rust_doctor::structure::oversized_unit reports the same defect and also names the oversized files, impl blocks and modules that a per-function lint cannot see.
Denied by default in the toolchain: the same refusal applies, and a scan has no way to lower a denied lint back to a warning.
